skills.title: Read and write 5- and 6-digit numbers in numerals and words
Place commas the Indian way (thousands, lakhs)
Compare and order 5- and 6-digit numbers using place value

expectations: Each place is 10 times the place to its right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, lakhs
A zero holds an empty place, so 10,500 is ten thousand five hundred, not one thousand five hundred
In the Indian system the first comma comes after 3 digits from the right (thousands), then after every 2 digits (lakhs)
A number with more digits is bigger; with the same number of digits, compare from the leftmost place
1,00,000 (one lakh) is the smallest 6-digit number and is 10 times 10,000

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the comma is decorative and can go anywhere in the number
signs: Puts a comma every 3 digits from the left
Cannot say what place a comma marks

skills.title: Round numbers to the nearest 10, 100 and 1000
Estimate sums and differences of large numbers by rounding
Choose a sensible rounding place and say when an estimate is enough

expectations: Rounding gives an 'about' number; the real amount does not change
Look only at the digit just right of the rounding place: 5 or more rounds up, less than 5 rounds down
A number exactly halfway (like 45,500 to the nearest thousand) rounds up
To estimate a sum or difference, round each number first, then add or subtract
Pick the rounding place that keeps the estimate useful for the job (nearest 100 km for a trip plan)

misconceptions.belief: Believes rounding changes the actual amount (the road really becomes 5,000 km)
signs: Says the trip got longer after rounding
Uses the rounded number as the exact answer for money or tickets
Refuses to round because 'it will be wrong'

skills.title: Mark unit fractions on a number line by splitting 0 to 1 into equal gaps

expectations: Fractions are numbers, so they have places on the number line between and beyond whole numbers

The top number tells how many gaps to count from 0
A fraction with a bigger top than bottom, like 5/4, lies beyond 1

misconceptions.belief: Thinks fractions are not numbers and cannot go on the number line
signs: Says there is nothing between 0 and 1
Treats a fraction as two separate numbers

skills.title: Read the height of a bar using the scale
